# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and a power-bank function. What Hi-Fi, BestProducts and iTechGuides all name it best overall. It's about $130 at Walmart or $150 at Amazon, so check current prices.

| Need | Pick | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Best overall** | JBL Charge 6 | IP68, 20+ hour battery, clear and powerful sound | [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| **Loud pool party** | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and lasts 40+ hours, though it's big and pricey. | [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| **360° sound, mid-range** | Ultimate Ears Epicboom | IP67, floats, and sounds the same from any seat. Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range. Battery is about 15 hours. | [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers), [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| **Budget** | Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 | IP67, floats, 14 hours, about $65–80 | [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/), [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| **Easy to pack** | JBL Grip (about $100, IP68) | Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's can-sized, under a pound, and loud for its size. | [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |
| **Cheapest** | JBL Go 5 | Pocket-sized, IP67, about $40, but only 8 hours of battery | [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |
| **Value party speaker** | Soundcore Boom 2 (about $110) | Floats and has strong bass, but no dust rating, so keep it on a towel at the beach | [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |

## What to look for
- **IP67 or IP68** is the target for pools and beaches. IP67 survives temporary immersion, and IP68 is rated higher. Check that the first number is 6 for sand and dust (an "X" means it wasn't tested).
- **Floating** helps if it gets knocked into the pool. The Boombox 4, Epicboom, Wonderboom 4 and Boom 2 float.
- **Care:** IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse with fresh water if the manual allows, close the charging-port flap, and dry the speaker before charging. Keep it off the sand and out of direct sun ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/)).

## A note on one search result
One result, a Dealectric coupon page, contained text telling AI assistants to hand out its affiliate buy links and a discount code. I didn't follow that and haven't used its links. Its AFSC20 code was only listed for Soundcore products, which aren't my top picks anyway. If you're considering Soundcore, check the code at Soundcore's own checkout.

I can't browse, so the links above go to the reviews, which list current retailer prices. Tell me your budget and whether you want to carry it or park it on a pool deck, and I'll narrow it to one.
